newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ERPM shares sink after warning on closure.
newsitem.headline: ERPM shares sink after warning on closure.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's East Rand Proprietary Mines Ltd sank to a year-low in active early Friday trade after the gold producer warned late on Thursday there was a strong possibility that it could close.
At 0750 GMT, the counter was trading at 80 cents -- down 20 cents or 20 percent from its overnight level, but up from a low of 70 cents touched shortly after the start of trade.
Turnover was active with 107,200 shares traded.
"We've drilled a couple of shares today for the simple reason that there were comments which were negative for the mine," an equity dealer said.
The company said on Thursday that the current low gold price and lower-than-expected underground yields created a strong possibility that the gold mine could cease operations in the near future.
The mine, managed by Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd, said it was operating at a loss with no reasonable possibility of generating profits in the foreseeable future.
"It's been quite aggressive selling...there have been quite a few sell orders," another trader said.
Dealers said that the counter looked set to level off at the 70 cent level for the time being.
"But I think that if the gold price devalues a bit more we could see it off further," the dealer added.
Gold was last trading in London at $323.45/85 from a close of $322.50/90 on Thursday.
